question.text: A vector has magnitude same as that of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi mathvariant="italic">A</mi><mo mathvariant="italic">→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math> and is parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi mathvariant="italic">B</mi><mo mathvariant="italic">→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>. The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math> components of this vector in first quadrant are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> respectively where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>=</mo></math>____.

solution.text:
Magnitude of vector A→=32+42=5

Now, unit vector along B→=(4i^+3j^)42+32=45i^+35j^

Now, N→=A→B^=5×45i^+35j^=4i^+3j^

∴x=4
